organizing_principle: the judgmental (doxa/belief) vs. non-judgmental (phantasia/appearance) debate on Aristotelian pathos
purpose: secondary-literature backbone for tmp/Dissertation/Section-5-Emotion-ADVISOR-REVIEW-2026-06-04.md (esp. T1-2, T1-4, animal-pathos)
content_filter: no >=25-word verbatim from any unit; paraphrase + page anchor only

units.author: Fortenbaugh, W. W.
units.title: Aristotle on Emotion: A Contribution to Philosophical Psychology, Rhetoric, Poetics, Politics, and Ethics
units.pdf: corpus/rhetorical_ontology/Fortenbaugh, W. W. - Aristotle on Emotion_(1975)_[clean copy].pdf
units.scope: whole (short); core = emotion-as-cognition, emotion vs belief/appearance, effect of emotion on judgment, pleasure/pain
units.signature_thesis: Aristotle's advance over Plato: emotions essentially involve a belief/judgment and are therefore answerable to reason and to rhetorical persuasion
units.role_for_dissertation: ALLY for the doxa-gate (T1-2): the belief-view pedigree the thesis refines

units.author: Konstan, David
units.title: The Emotions of the Ancient Greeks: Studies in Aristotle and Classical Literature
units.publisher: University of Toronto Press (Robson Classical Lectures)
units.pdf: corpus/rhetorical_ontology/Konstan, David - The Emotions of the Ancient Greeks_(2009)_[clean copy].pdf
units.signature_thesis: Greek pathe differ from modern emotions; they are construals of others' acts/intentions bearing on social standing; emotions are judgments, changeable by persuasion, and denied 'in the proper sense' to animals and small children
units.role_for_dissertation: ALLY (social-cognitive); arms toward-whom/Mitsein (element 2), animal-pathos (1079 fn), and T1-4 via the Grief chapter

units.author: Moss, Jessica
units.title: Akrasia and Perceptual Illusion
units.pdf: corpus/rhetorical_ontology/Moss, Jessica - Akrasia and Perceptual Illusion_(2009)_[clean copy].pdf
units.scope: whole article; = published form of Moss-AG Ch. 5
units.signature_thesis: akrasia (NE VII.3) is a conflict between phantasia and rational cognition, structurally parallel to perceptual illusion; the motivating evaluative appearance is non-doxastic and can run contrary to belief (the sun looks a foot wide though we believe it vast)
units.role_for_dissertation: RIVAL (T1-2): the illusion model IS the recalcitrance argument against a doxa-requirement

units.author: Moss, Jessica
units.title: Aristotle on the Apparent Good: Perception, Phantasia, Thought, and Desire
units.pdf: corpus/rhetorical_ontology/Moss, Jessica - Aristotle on the Apparent Good- Perception, Phantasia, Thought, and Desire_(2012)_[clean copy].pdf
scope_chapters: 5 Akrasia and the Apparent Good (100-136, = aes-03)
key_subsections: 4.1 Doxastic vs. phantastic accounts of the passions (70)
4.5 First doxastic objection: the contents of perception (87)
4.6 Second doxastic objection: accepting vs. believing (90)
4.7-4.8 Aristotle and the Stoics on phantasia, assent, passion, belief (92-99)
units.signature_thesis: the apparent good (phainomenon agathon) is a literal quasi-perceptual appearance via phantasia, not a rational belief; the passions are explained on the phantastic (not doxastic) model
units.role_for_dissertation: RIVAL (T1-2) + the named 'doxastic vs phantastic' framing for the whole debate; also bears on apparent-good claim at diss 1060

units.author: Dow, Jamie
units.title: Passions and Persuasion in Aristotle's Rhetoric
units.pdf: corpus/rhetorical_ontology/Dow, Jamie - Passions and Persuasion in Aristotle's Rhetoric_(2015)_[clean copy].pdf
units.scope: the 'Feeling Fantastic Again - Passions, Appearances, and Beliefs' chapter + the chapter(s) defining passions as pleasures/pains with a cognitive (affirmation) component
units.signature_thesis: the passions are pleasures/pains with a cognitive component; the phantasia involved requires the subject AFFIRMING things to be as represented (against the 'mere appearance' reading), which lets aroused passions count as reasonable acceptance of premises
units.role_for_dissertation: ALLY (T1-2): Dow's 'affirmation' ~ the thesis's 'taking-as-true'; his defense vs recalcitrance is the resource to mine; check whether his affirmation = full doxa
